mainTopic: How rules pass between the חטאות: the יום הכפורים offerings, the communal bull, and שעירי עבודה זרה, and the limits on learning from a היקש
overview: The amud opens with the end of a קל וחומר from תנא דבי רבי ישמעאל. That קל וחומר teaches that the פר and שעיר of יום הכפורים follow the dipping rules of את, בדם and טבילה. The גמרא asks how a rule learned by a היקש can go on to teach by קל וחומר. רב פפא answers that this תנא allows it. Next the גמרא asks why the ברייתא needs the word "לפר" for פר העלם דבר של צבור. רב פפא explains that it makes the burning of the יותרת and two כליות count as written about that bull directly. That way the bull can teach it to שעירי עבודה זרה without one היקש teaching through another היקש. A ברייתא supports him, reading "חטאתם על שגגתם" in במדבר as linking the goats to the communal bull. Finally the גמרא asks why "חטאתם" is needed when "החטאת" already included the goats, and רב פפא begins an answer that continues on the next amud.

steps.title: Finishing the קל וחומר and applying it to יום הכפורים
steps.stepSummary: The קל וחומר ends with the point that the פר and שעיר of יום הכפורים share the same blood actions. So the פר of יום הכפורים learns את, בדם and טבילה from פר כהן משיח, and the שעיר of יום הכפורים learns them from שעירי עבודה זרה.
steps.simpleTranslation: ...since their actions are made equal to each other! So the bull of יום הכפורים learns the rules of את, בדם and טבילה from the bull of the anointed כהן. And the goat of יום הכפורים learns them from the goats brought for communal עבודה זרה, through a קל וחומר.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא finishes a קל וחומר that began earlier and then spells out what it teaches: the יום הכפורים offerings learn the dipping rules from other offerings.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The key point of the קל וחומר is that the פר and שעיר of יום הכפורים have their blood actions equated with each other. Because of that, each one learns את, בדם and טבילה from its matching offering. The bull learns from a bull (פר כהן משיח), and the goat learns from goats (שעירי עבודה זרה).

keyTerms.meaning: the actions (of sprinkling the blood) were made equal to each other
the bull brought by the כהן גדול for his mistaken sin

a logical argument from a lighter case to a stronger one

steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: The פר of יום הכפורים learns את, בדם and טבילה from פר כהן משיח. The שעיר of יום הכפורים learns them from שעירי עבודה זרה, through a קל וחומר.

steps.title: Can something learned by a היקש go on to teach by קל וחומר?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges the derivation for the שעיר of יום הכפורים. The goats of עבודה זרה only got these rules through a היקש, so how can they pass them on through a קל וחומר?
steps.simpleTranslation: But can a matter that was learned through a היקש turn around and teach something else through a קל וחומר?!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא attacks the second half of step 1, where the שעיר of יום הכפורים learned from שעירי עבודה זרה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The dipping rules are not written directly about שעירי עבודה זרה; those goats only received them through a היקש, a comparison between offerings. There is a known rule that, with קדשים, something learned through a היקש cannot then teach further by קל וחומר. So the chain of learning in step 1 seems to break.

keyTerms.meaning: a comparison the תורה makes between two cases, so that one learns from the other
a law that is learned, not written directly
turns around and teaches something else

phrases.english: But can a matter that is learned through a juxtaposition,
phrases.notes: The goats of עבודה זרה only got these dipping rules through a comparison. The rules aren't written about the goats directly.

phrases.english: turn around and teach through a kal vachomer?!

steps.triggerLanguage: וְכִי דָּבָר הַלָּמֵד בְּהֶיקֵּשׁ, חוֹזֵר וּמְלַמֵּד בְּקַל וָחוֹמֶר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the method used in step 1 for the שעיר of יום הכפורים.
steps.kashyaTarget: The learning of the שעיר of יום הכפורים from שעירי עבודה זרה
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: שעירי עבודה זרה got these rules only through a היקש. Something learned through a היקש cannot normally teach again through a קל וחומר.

steps.title: This תנא holds that a היקש-learned rule can teach by קל וחומר
steps.stepSummary: רב פפא answers that תנא דבי רבי ישמעאל holds a rule learned through a היקש can go on to teach through a קל וחומר.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב פפא said: תנא דבי רבי ישמעאל holds that a matter learned through a היקש does turn around and teach through a קל וחומר.
steps.whatsHappening: רב פפא answers the challenge. The ברייתא's author simply holds the other opinion about this rule.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא's derivation is not wrong. It follows the view of its own author, תנא דבי רבי ישמעאל. He allows a rule learned through a היקש to teach again through a קל וחומר, so the chain of learning in step 1 holds up.

keyTerms.meaning: he holds, his view is
the תנא of the school of רבי ישמעאל

steps.whatToRemember: According to תנא דבי רבי ישמעאל, a rule learned through a היקש can still teach through a קל וחומר. That is why the שעיר of יום הכפורים can learn from שעירי עבודה זרה.

phrases.english: Rav Pappa said:
The tanna of the school of Rabbi Yishmael holds:
a matter learned through a juxtaposition

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב פָּפָּא: קָסָבַר תָּנָא דְּבֵי רַבִּי יִשְׁמָעֵאל

steps.terutzMaskana: תנא דבי רבי ישמעאל holds that it can, so his derivation stands.

steps.title: Quoting the ברייתא: "לפר" is the communal bull
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא goes back to the ברייתא and quotes its reading: the word "לפר" refers to פר העלם דבר של צבור.
steps.simpleTranslation: "לפר" (to the bull) — this is the bull for the community's mistaken ruling.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is setting up its next question by quoting another line from the ברייתא of תנא דבי רבי ישמעאל.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא reads the word "לפר" in the פסוק as pointing to פר העלם דבר של צבור. The גמרא quotes it here only to question it in the next step.

keyTerms.meaning: the bull brought when the community sins by following a mistaken ruling of the court

phrases.aramaic: ״לַפָּר״ – זֶה פַּר הֶעְלֵם דָּבָר שֶׁל צִבּוּר.
phrases.english: "With the bull" – this is the bull for an unwitting communal sin.

steps.triggerLanguage: ״לַפָּר״ – זֶה פַּר הֶעְלֵם דָּבָר שֶׁל צִבּוּר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Leaves the היקש question behind and returns to a different line of the ברייתא.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The word "לפר" refers to פר העלם דבר של צבור.

steps.title: Why do we need a word to teach this, if the פסוק is about that bull?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks why the ברייתא needs "לפר" to teach about פר העלם דבר של צבור. The פסוק itself is written in the section about that very bull.
steps.simpleTranslation: But this פסוק is itself written about the communal bull!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the ברייתא's reading from step 4 as unneeded.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק is in the section of פר העלם דבר של צבור, so its laws obviously apply to that bull. Using a special word to point to it seems pointless.

keyTerms.meaning: itself
it is written

phrases.english: But this is written about the community itself!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the reading quoted in step 4.
steps.kashyaTarget: The ברייתא's reading of "לפר" as פר העלם דבר של צבור
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The פסוק already speaks about that bull directly, so a special reading teaches nothing new.

steps.title: The communal bull needs to pass the fats on to the goats of עבודה זרה
steps.stepSummary: רב פפא explains the reason for the reading. The ברייתא wants פר העלם דבר של צבור to teach the burning of the יותרת and two כליות to שעירי עבודה זרה.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב פפא said: Because the ברייתא wants to teach from the communal bull, about the יותרת and the two כליות, to the goats of עבודה זרה.
steps.whatsHappening: רב פפא answers step 5 by showing that "לפר" has a real job to do.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The reading is not just telling us that the פסוק applies to the communal bull. It makes פר העלם דבר של צבור the source that passes on the burning of the יותרת and two כליות. Those parts are then carried over to שעירי עבודה זרה, even though this is not written about the goats.

keyTerms.meaning: to teach, to pass on a law
the lobe of the liver (also called the diaphragm), one of the parts burned on the מזבח
the two kidneys, burned on the מזבח

steps.whatToRemember: The word "לפר" turns פר העלם דבר של צבור into a source that teaches the burning of the יותרת and two כליות to שעירי עבודה זרה.
steps.whyThisMatters: It shows that the ברייתא's readings are never extra. Even a reading that looks obvious is there to set up a chain of learning between offerings.

phrases.english: Rav Pappa said:
Because he wants to teach
from the bull for an unwitting communal sin
about the diaphragm and the two kidneys,
phrases.notes: These are parts burned on the מזבח. The point is that this burning isn't written about the goats.

phrases.english: to the goats brought for idol worship.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב פָּפָּא: מִשּׁוּם דְּבָעֵי אַגְמוֹרֵי
steps.terutzResolutionType: Gives the reading a new purpose
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The reading seemed to just tell us the פסוק applies to the communal bull, which is obvious.
steps.terutzMaskana: The reading makes the communal bull a teacher, so it can pass the burning of the יותרת and two כליות on to שעירי עבודה זרה.

steps.title: Why the word "with the bull" is needed: to avoid a double היקש
steps.stepSummary: רב פפא finishes his answer. The rule for פר העלם דבר של צבור only comes through a היקש. So "לפר" makes it count as if it were written about that bull directly. This way the bull can teach שעירי עבודה זרה without a היקש coming from a היקש.
steps.simpleTranslation: The burning of the יותרת and kidneys is not written about פר העלם דבר של צבור itself. It only comes to it through a היקש. So the תורה needed to write "with the bull" to make it count as if it were written about that bull directly. Otherwise, when this bull teaches the goats, we would have something learned by היקש going on to teach by היקש.
steps.whatsHappening: רב פפא is finishing his explanation of why the ברייתא needs the word "לפר".
steps.deeperAnalysis: The rule about the יותרת and כליות is written in the section of the פר כהן משיח. פר העלם דבר של צבור only gets it through a היקש. If that bull then taught שעירי עבודה זרה through another היקש, that would be a double היקש, which is not allowed in קדשים. The word "לפר" makes the rule count as written directly about this bull, so the problem goes away.

keyTerms.meaning: It is not written about this case itself
A link the Torah makes between two topics, so that one learns its rules from the other
It was needed

keyTerms.term: דָּבָר הַלָּמֵד בְּהֶיקֵּשׁ חוֹזֵר וּמְלַמֵּד בְּהֶיקֵּשׁ
keyTerms.meaning: Something learned through a היקש that then teaches something else through a היקש

steps.confusionAlert: Do not mix this up with Step 3. There, a rule learned by היקש was allowed to teach through a קל וחומר. Here the problem is different: a rule learned by היקש cannot teach through another היקש.
steps.whyThisMatters: This shows a basic rule of learning in קדשים: you cannot chain one היקש onto another. A single extra word can be used to get around this.

phrases.english: And the bull for an unwitting communal sin –

phrases.english: it comes through a היקש;
so "with the bull" was needed –

steps.title: A ברייתא supports רב פפא and asks why "with the bull" is written
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא brings a ברייתא that agrees with רב פפא. The ברייתא opens by asking why the פסוק "ועשה כאשר עשה" needs to say "לפר".
steps.simpleTranslation: A ברייתא was taught that agrees with רב פפא: "And he shall do as he did." Why does the פסוק need to say "with the bull"?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא to support רב פפא. Here it only quotes the ברייתא's opening question; the answer comes in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא asks the same question as Step 5: why write "לפר" when it is obvious the פסוק is about the bull? Asking this shows that the ברייתא also sees "לפר" as extra and expects it to teach something new. That matches רב פפא.

keyTerms.meaning: A ברייתא was taught that agrees with him
Why does the פסוק need to say this?
"And he shall do as he did" (said about פר העלם דבר של צבור)

phrases.english: It was taught in a ברייתא in line with רב פפא:
"And he shall do as he did" –
why does the verse say "with the bull"?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Brings a ברייתא to back up רב פפא's explanation from Steps 6 and 7.
steps.raayaObject: רב פפא's claim that "לפר" is there so that פר העלם דבר של צבור can teach שעירי עבודה זרה
steps.raayaSupportSource: A ברייתא on ויקרא 4:20 that asks the same question about "לפר"

steps.title: The ברייתא links the goats of עבודה זרה to the communal bull
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא begins its answer with a פסוק about the goats. "חטאתם" means שעירי עבודה זרה, and "שגגתם" means פר העלם דבר של צבור. So the goats must be treated like the bull.
steps.simpleTranslation: Because it says: "And they brought their offering, a fire-offering to ה׳." "Their sin offering" means שעירי עבודה זרה. "Their error" means פר העלם דבר של צבור. "Their sin offering for their error": the תורה is saying that their sin offering should be treated like their error.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא starts answering its question. It shows from a פסוק in במדבר that the goats of עבודה זרה are compared to פר העלם דבר של צבור.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא reads two words in the פסוק as two different offerings. "חטאתם" means the goats, and "שגגתם" means the communal bull. The phrase "חטאתם על שגגתם" tells us the goats follow the bull's rules. This sets up why the bull needs "לפר": it is the one teaching the goats.

keyTerms.meaning: The goats brought by the community for an unwitting sin of idol worship
"Their sin offering", read here as the goats
"Their error", read here as פר העלם דבר של צבור

phrases.english: Because it says:
"And they brought their offering
a fire-offering to ה׳, etc."
"their sin offering" – these are the goats for idol worship,

phrases.english: "their error" – this is the bull for an unwitting communal sin,
"their sin offering for their error" –
the Torah is saying:
their sin offering is, for you, like their error;
phrases.notes: He means the goats are treated like the bull for the parts burned on the מזבח.

steps.triggerLanguage: לְפִי שֶׁנֶּאֱמַר וְהֵם הֵבִיאוּ אֶת קׇרְבָּנָם

steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: A פסוק in במדבר links שעירי עבודה זרה ("חטאתם") to פר העלם דבר של צבור ("שגגתם"), so the goats take on the bull's rules.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Why the פסוק needs to say "לפר"

steps.title: The community bull only learned its rule through a comparison
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא challenges itself: the community bull learned the burning of the fats through a היקש, so how can it pass that rule on to the goats through another היקש?
steps.simpleTranslation: Where did you learn this rule for the community bull? Was it not through a היקש? But can something learned through a היקש turn around and teach through a היקש?
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא raises a problem with its own reasoning. The goats are supposed to learn from the community bull, but that bull only got the rule through a comparison.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The burning of the יותרת and כליות is not written about פר העלם דבר של צבור. It only got it by a היקש from פר כהן משיח. The rule is that a law learned by a היקש cannot be used to teach another case through a second היקש, so the chain seems to break.

keyTerms.meaning: 'Their error.' Here it means the bull brought for the community's mistake
From where did you learn it?

keyTerms.term: דָּבָר הַלָּמֵד בְּהֶיקֵּשׁ חוֹזֵר וּמְלַמֵּד בְּהֶיקֵּשׁ
keyTerms.meaning: Something learned through a היקש teaching again through a היקש. This is not allowed in קדשים

phrases.english: Their error — from where did you learn it?
phrases.notes: 'Their error' is the community bull from the פסוק in the last step.

phrases.english: Was it not through a juxtaposition?
phrases.notes: The community bull got its fat rules by being compared to the anointed priest's bull.

phrases.english: But does something learned through a juxtaposition

steps.triggerLanguage: וְכִי דָּבָר הַלָּמֵד בְּהֶיקֵּשׁ חוֹזֵר וּמְלַמֵּד בְּהֶיקֵּשׁ

steps.kashyaTarget: The ברייתא's claim in step 9 that the goats learn from פר העלם דבר של צבור.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The bull's own rule comes only from a היקש, and a rule learned by a היקש cannot teach again by a היקש.

steps.title: The double word 'with the bull' makes the rule count as written directly
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא answers from the פסוק 'ועשה לפר כאשר עשה לפר'. The first 'לפר' is the community bull and the second is the bull of the כהן משיח, so the rule counts as written about the community bull itself.
steps.simpleTranslation: The פסוק says 'with the bull.' This is the community bull. Then it says 'with the bull' again. This is the bull of the anointed כהן.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא solves its own problem using the extra word 'לפר', exactly as רב פפא said in step 7.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Because the פסוק names both bulls, the burning of the fats is treated as if it were written about פר העלם דבר של צבור directly. So the bull is now a 'first-hand' source. It can teach שעירי עבודה זרה through a single היקש, which is allowed.

keyTerms.meaning: The פסוק teaches. Used to bring the source that solves a problem
'With the bull.' This word appears twice in ויקרא 4:20
The bull brought by the anointed כהן גדול for his mistake

steps.whatToRemember: The extra 'לפר' turns a rule that came second-hand into one that counts as written directly. That way the community bull can teach the goats without a היקש coming from a היקש. This is the proof for רב פפא.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 10 and completes the ברייתא's support for רב פפא.
steps.terutzResolutionType: A פסוק that turns a היקש-based rule into one that counts as written directly
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The community bull's rule comes only through a היקש, so it could not teach the goats.
steps.terutzMaskana: 'לפר' links the two bulls directly. The rule counts as written about the community bull, so it can teach the goats.

steps.title: Why is 'their sin offering' needed if the goats were already included?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the ברייתא's reading 'חטאתם' = שעירי עבודה זרה. It asks why this is needed, since an earlier ברייתא already included the goats from the word 'החטאת'.
steps.simpleTranslation: The Master said: 'Their sin offering' means שעירי עבודה זרה. But let him learn this from the earlier פסוק! The Master said there: 'The sin offering' comes to include שעירי עבודה זרה.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא goes back to a line from the ברייתא and asks why the goats need a new source when they already have one.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Earlier (39b) a ברייתא learned from 'החטאת' in ויקרא 4:20 that שעירי עבודה זרה are included with the community bull. If so, the word 'חטאתם' seems extra. Why does the תורה need two sources for the same goats?

keyTerms.meaning: Let him derive it from a different source

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Goes back to the ברייתא's reading from step 9 and questions whether it is needed.
steps.kashyaTarget: The ברייתא's reading that 'חטאתם' refers to שעירי עבודה זרה.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The goats were already included by 'החטאת', so a second source seems extra.

steps.title: The earlier source might have covered only the sprinklings
steps.stepSummary: רב פפא says the second source was needed. Without it, one might think the earlier 'החטאת' links the goats only for the sprinklings of blood, which are written about the community bull itself.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב פפא said: It was needed. You might have thought that this applies only to the sprinklings, which are written about the bull itself.
steps.whatsHappening: רב פפא begins his answer to why the goats need two sources. His explanation continues on the next amud.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The sprinklings of blood are written directly in the section of פר העלם דבר של צבור. So one might think 'החטאת' only tells the goats to copy those. 'חטאתם' is then needed to teach the burning of the fats, which the bull itself only had through 'לפר'.

keyTerms.meaning: It was needed
It would have entered your mind to say. This introduces a mistaken assumption
The sprinklings of the blood
In its own section, written directly about it

steps.confusionAlert: רב פפא is not saying the earlier 'החטאת' was wrong. He is saying it might have covered only the sprinklings, so a second word is needed for the fats.
